lines.text: I'm Bean, a little gray afternoon
I've got a blanket and a patch of room
No great adventure on my mind
I've left that sort of thing behind
You step toward me; I tiptoe away
Another cushion. Same lovely day
I've been awake for several minutes
You're still dreaming; I don't get it
I wait beside you, then I move
My little face right next to you
A purr, a meow, a second review
You chose a Bean. You knew what to do
I'm not upset; I'm asking you
Did we forget that breakfast was due?
You stir; I follow down the hall
That little silver lid says it all
One soft click, and I know it's true
My favorite kind of love comes through
Breakfast was due
And the morning came through
Warm in my corner, with nothing to prove
A bowl of something lovely
A blanket made for two
A little space, a little grace
And love that lets me choose
Breakfast was due
Salmon, tuna, chicken too
I hear that can and fall for you
Your boys leave kibble; I believe
Good food was never meant to grieve
They call me Foopa Master; fair
I wear them round and doing fine
The soft life suits this shape of mine
My brothers bring their big ideas
I hiss; they don't appear to hear
I lose, then find another seat
My afternoon was going well
I've nothing more to prove or tell
I may step back when you come near
It doesn't mean I want you gone
At night I climb the blanket here
And press my little paws along
I know it's you beneath the fold
I like the quiet that we share
I needn't ask for you to hold me
I like knowing you are there
Was that the kitchen?
Breakfast was due
And the morning came through
Warm in my corner, with nothing to prove
My bowl is empty now
My brothers found something to do
A little space, a little grace
And love that lets me choose
I'm your Foopa Master
With a blanket and a view
Breakfast was due
I curl up, then I tiptoe free
You lift me: I'm the Dancing Queen
I had intended just to sit
I suppose I'll live with it
...Clarence Thomas.
